sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how Java remembers where your objects live in memory? Let's explore reference variables!

• What reference variables really are
• How they point to objects in memory
• The difference between objects and references
• Common pitfalls to avoid

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine reference variables like sticky notes on a fridge. The fridge is your computer's memory, and the sticky note (reference variable) tells you where to find the milk (object).

When you create an object in Java, it lives somewhere in memory. A reference variable is just a name that points to that memory location.

• Think of it like a phone number - the number isn't the person, but it lets you reach them
• Multiple reference variables can point to the same object
• A reference variable with value 'null' points to nothing (like a blank sticky note)

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Accessing Objects via Reference Variables works:

steps.title: Creating an Object
steps.description: When you create an object, Java allocates memory for it and gives you a reference.

steps.title: Reference Assignment
steps.description: The reference variable 'john' now points to the Person object in memory.
steps.code: Person friend = john; // Both point to same object!

steps.title: Modifying Through Reference
steps.description: Changes made through either reference affect the same object.

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Reference variables store memory addresses, not objects themselves
✓ Multiple references can point to the same object
✓ Changing an object through one reference affects all references to it
✓ 'null' means the reference points to nothing
✓ The '==' operator compares references, not object contents

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Initialize reference variables to avoid NullPointerException
Use .equals() to compare object contents, not '=='
Set references to null when done to help garbage collection
donts: Don't assume two references point to different objects
Don't forget to check for null before calling methods
Don't confuse reference assignment with object copying
sections.protip: When you pass objects to methods, you're passing references - changes inside the method affect the original object!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Accessing Objects via Reference Variables used in real apps?

examples.how: User objects are passed around via references - when you update your profile, all parts of the app see the changes
Game entities (players, enemies) are referenced throughout the game - moving one reference updates all views

problem.description:
Create a simple BankAccount class with balance. Then:
1. Create two reference variables pointing to the same account
2. Deposit money through one reference
3. Check balance through the other reference
4. What do you observe?
hints: Remember: both references point to the same object!
Try printing the balance after each operation
problem.explanation: Both account1 and account2 reference the same BankAccount object. When you modify the object through one reference, the change is visible through all references to that object.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Reference variables are like pointers to objects in memory
📌 Multiple references can point to the same object
📌 Practice creating and using reference variables to understand object sharing
📌 Ready to learn about object copying and cloning next!
